traits.body_plan.note: About 86% of liverwort species are leafy; the complex thalloids (about 6%) and the simple thalloids (about 8%) make up the rest (Wikström, He-Nygrén and Shaw 2009).

traits.leaf_bearing.note: The leafy liverworts, about 86% of the species, bear leaves; the thalloid ones, the rest, have a thallus instead (Wikström, He-Nygrén and Shaw 2009).

traits.anchorage.note: Liverworts hold to their ground by rhizoids, single cells in all but a few species (Australian Bryophytes, 'What is a liverwort?').

traits.reproduction.note: Liverworts spread by spores, shed from the capsule of the sporophyte that grows from the plant (Australian Bryophytes).

traits.sporangia.note: A liverwort's spores form in a capsule, which a short-lived stalk, the seta, lifts from the plant before it splits (Australian Bryophytes).
